tournament.title: Oral Small-Molecule & Macrocycle PCSK9 Inhibitors in ASCVD
tournament.goal: Evaluate oral allosteric small-molecule and tricyclic macrocycle PCSK9 inhibitors disrupting LDLR EGF-A binding in ASCVD.

preferences: Prioritize oral bioavailability and hepatocyte target engagement
Enforce human loss-of-function genetic validation (PCSK9 R46L / LoF)

claims.claim: PCSK9 loss-of-function variants confer 88% reduction in coronary heart disease risk without adverse hepatic phenotypes.
claims.source_sentence: Loss-of-function mutations in PCSK9 lower LDL-C and protect against CHD.
claims.reasoning: Directly supported by Cohen et al. NEJM 2006 (PMID:16554528).

references.title: Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease

claims.claim: The PCSK9 catalytic/C-terminal groove forms a druggable pocket distinct from the flat EGF-A interface.
claims.source_sentence: Crystallographic analysis reveals a cryptic pocket adjacent to the catalytic triad.
claims.reasoning: Supported by structural studies of PCSK9 small-molecule complexes.

prose.summary: Small-molecule engagement of the inter-domain allosteric groove between the PCSK9 catalytic and C-terminal Cys-His-rich domains allosterically destabilizes the LDLR EGF-A interface.
prose.description: Avoids the flat EGF-A PPI surface while preserving oral Rule-of-5 hepatocyte permeability. Tested via fpocket & AlphaFold 3 co-folding of PCSK9 (PDB 3P5B / Q8NBP7) to verify cryptic pocket druggability >= 0.50 and interface ipTM >= 0.75.
prose.reviews_summary: Strong human genetic validation (PCSK9 LoF cardioprotection) and superior oral druggability compared to orthosteric EGF-A surface binders.
prose.verification_summary: All 3 primary genetic and structural claims verified against Open Targets, gnomAD, and PDB 3P5B.

claims.source_sentence: MK-0616 binds PCSK9 and blocks LDLR interaction.
claims.reasoning: Supported by Ballantyne et al. JACC 2023 (PMID:36884306).

references.title: Phase 2b trial of oral PCSK9 macrocycle MK-0616

prose.summary: Oral tricyclic peptidomimetic macrocycle directly occluding the PCSK9 EGF-A binding patch.
prose.description: Direct orthosteric competition with LDLR EGF-A domain benchmarked against clinical macrocycle MK-0616.
prose.reviews_summary: Clinically validated mechanism (MK-0616), retained as backup concept due to higher molecular weight and permeation enhancer requirements.
prose.verification_summary: Orthosteric EGF-A blockade claims verified against PDB 3P5B and MK-0616 clinical data.

knowledge_base.summary: PCSK9 binds the EGF-A domain of LDLR on hepatocyte surfaces, routing LDLR to lysosomal degradation.

report.overview: Tournament evaluated small-molecule allosteric and macrocyclic orthosteric strategies for oral PCSK9 inhibition.
report.top_ideas_summary:
## Recommendation and Best Next Steps
Advance H-001 (IC-001, allosteric small-molecule PCSK9 inhibitor, Elo 1642.5) as primary series and H-002 (IC-002, oral macrocycle, Elo 1588.0) as backup series into Stage 1 genetic, transcriptomic, and structural validation.
report.reviews_overview: Reviewers favored H-001 for classical oral small-molecule Rule-of-5 properties without permeation enhancers.
